svg.text: Moved out of Fetch_Control into EX
Dots are junctions; plain crossings are not connected.
adder1, mux1, mux2 stay in IF. They work on the PC.
adder2 moves to EX, because s_PC_EX and s_immgen_EX only exist there.
org1 and jalr_target can stay inside Fetch_Control, but they are driven by EX_MEM,
so they act on MEM-stage values. Stage = which register feeds it, not where it is drawn.
Branch, jal and jalr all redirect the PC while they are in MEM.
BRANCH_U sits in EX, and its result is registered as s_pcsrc_MEM.
A signal keeps its old name in the stage that creates it.
Each register it crosses adds the next stage: s_read2, s_read2_EX, s_read2_MEM.
The testbench reads the unsuffixed names, so they mark the final stage:
s_DMemWr, s_DMemAddr, s_DMemData, s_DMemBE are the MEM versions.
s_RegWr, s_RegWrAddr, s_RegWrData, s_Halt are the WB versions.
s_Inst stays the IMem output in IF.
Software rules (no forwarding, no hazard detection)
Data hazard: 2 NOPs between an instruction that writes a register and one that reads it.
G_REG_CLK inverts the REGS clock: writes land on the falling edge, mid-cycle.
So a reader in ID sees the value in the second half of the writer's WB cycle.
Control hazard: 3 NOPs after every branch, jal and jalr.
They are fetched in the cycles before the PC redirect happens in MEM.
s_Halt is read in WB, so wfi lets the instructions before it finish.
